races.name: Party Time And Limerick Motor Centre Rated Race

runners_data.name: Alfred Tennyson
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up performer with recent Goodwood form at 6-7f on good, running for an in-form trainer (2/10 in 14 days); held up at the rear, will need this pace to be genuine to close ground, though Firm ground suits his turf profile.
runners_data.comment: Alfred Tennyson is winless in his last six starts but has been fairly consistent, with a second and a third among a mix of midfield finishes. Back only 15 days after his latest run and having covered today's trip before, he rates 78 with us, fifth of eleven from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Inishfallen
runners_data.note: Stephen Thorne's yard operating at a modest 1/3 strike rate over 14 days; drops to 6½f here but finished no better than 4th in his last four, and his hold-up style leaves him relying on late gaps that may not materialise in a sustainably-run race.
runners_data.comment: Inishfallen is yet to score in his last six starts and his form has tailed off — twice unplaced of late, with a second and two fourths earlier the pick. He returns just 14 days on, with today's trip already covered, rated 85 by us and a leading threat from stall 2, with the finish alone the query.

runners_data.name: Tokyo Treasure
runners_data.note: 273 days off the track is an immediate flag; carries a form note of fading in the finish and has an uncertain style profile, making him very hard to assess with confidence — the long absence and finishing tendency are both negatives.
runners_data.comment: Tokyo Treasure is winless in his last three starts and has been off the track for 273 days, a big question fitness-wise, though a third among those efforts and prior experience over today's trip offer some hope. Our rating of 71 leaves him ninth of eleven from stall 10.

runners_data.name: Clonmacash
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Adrian McGuinness (2/25 in 14 days) who showed a place effort last time over 6f; visor-wearing type who should settle close to Send Harry and is ideally profiled for a steady-tempo scenario where pressing the pace pays dividends.
runners_data.comment: Clonmacash won six starts back and has shown mixed form since, including a third among more modest efforts, and he returns just 14 days after his latest race over today's trip. Rated 80 by us, he's a leading threat from stall 7, fourth of eleven.

runners_data.name: Send Harry
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone pace-setter over his ideal 7f trip — dropping to 6½f here; his controlled style suits dictating, and with no one pressing him early the uncontested lead is his to exploit, though the trip is marginally shorter than his winning distance.
runners_data.comment: Send Harry won five starts back. He has run a pair of second-place efforts since, with a sixth and an unplaced run mixed in. He's back 23 days after his latest race over today's trip, rated 75 by us and seventh of eleven from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Apache Outlaw
runners_data.note: In truth a hold-up horse by habit, but with so many hold-up types in this field he has been mapped to midfield — he's unlikely to get a true rear-of-field position and his last two efforts (6f, STA/STA) show modest form; style dislocation is a genuine concern.
runners_data.comment: Apache Outlaw hasn't added to his tally in his last six starts but has stayed competitive throughout, headed by a third, with a track speed figure of 82 to his name. That form sees him rated 87 with us, the highest in this field, and he returns 15 days after his latest run over today's trip from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Morehampton
runners_data.note: JP Murtagh's 3-year-old with a useful yard strike rate of 4/19 over 14 days; genuine hold-up type based on form, and represents the most credible late-closer threat if the pace is honest, but runs from OR=79 — the highest in the field — which applies a significant weight burden.
runners_data.comment: Morehampton is yet to win in his last five starts, three of them unplaced, yet he's rated a lofty 86 with us, second of eleven on our figures. He returns 14 days after his latest race over today's trip from stall 3, with his inconsistent placing record the obvious knock.

runners_data.name: Western Bandit
runners_data.note: A 10f horse on the Flat being asked to run 6½f — the distance is a serious question mark; naturally held up at the rear but repositioned to midfield on the map due to field composition, and a combination of trip concern and style mismatch makes this a difficult proposition.
runners_data.comment: Western Bandit is yet to win in his last five starts, with a third his best form among a run of modest finishes. Back 19 days after his latest race, he rates only 68 with us, tenth of eleven from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Dancing Saxon
runners_data.note: Last won over 7f at Sligo and hasn't run since December (155-day absence); the JP O'Brien yard (8/55 in 14 days) gives confidence, and as a prominent type he slots neatly into the race's most favourable position — the layoff is the key unknown.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Saxon won last time out and has been a fair to middling finisher before that, with a fourth and a third among her other finishes. She's had a lengthy 155 days off since but has raced over today's trip previously, rated 78 by us and sixth of eleven from stall 9.

runners_data.name: Usuario Amigo
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse by nature, absorbed into the midfield map because the field is saturated with closers; recent form reads 9-7-7-7-10 on a rolling basis and he hasn't threatened a win in any of his last five, making him hard to back at any price in this company.
runners_data.comment: Usuario Amigo is yet to win in his last five starts, twice unplaced and no better than seventh otherwise. He returns 15 days after his latest race over today's trip, rated 72 by us, eighth of eleven from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Ocean Echo
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Mark Fahey who ran 2nd at Haydock over 7f on Heavy, though that surface is very different from today's Firm; maps forward here and could press Send Harry, giving him tactical relevance — the Firm ground on a tight 6½f is a step into the unknown.
runners_data.comment: Ocean Echo is yet to win in his last five starts, though a second in that spell shows he has ability, sandwiched between a run of modest finishes. Back 23 days after his latest race over today's trip, he's rated bottom of the field on 65 from stall 6.

races.paceDynamic: Send Harry is the confirmed lone front-runner and will press on from the gates, setting a sustainable gallop over 6½ furlongs on Firm ground at Limerick with no meaningful rival likely to dispute the lead — Clonmacash and Dancing Saxon are the most likely to track closely in second and third, while Ocean Echo may also attempt to go forward. With a single uncontested pace-setter dictating throughout, the race sets up as an end-to-end rhythm that will not collapse into a sprint finish but will instead reward horses who can travel close to the pace and sustain their effort into the closing stages. The field contains more genuine hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Apache Outlaw, Western Bandit, and Usuario Amigo are natural hold-up horses redistributed into midfield slots they are unlikely to occupy in practice, meaning any scenario that relies on a late closer's surge is undermined by the fact those horses are not true rear-of-field types in this race. This shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking racers who can latch onto Send Harry's controlled pace and grind past in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Send Harry Controls Clean
scenarios.trigger: If Send Harry leads unchallenged and the pace remains measured throughout, stamina-laden prominent types who travel close to the front will be perfectly positioned to pounce.
scenarios.body: Send Harry sets an honest but not suicidal gallop on Firm ground, and the horses immediately behind — Clonmacash and Dancing Saxon — get a dream stalking position and hit the rising ground with energy to spend.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Hit The Front
scenarios.trigger: If Clonmacash or Dancing Saxon move forward aggressively early and push Send Harry into a faster gallop than intended.
scenarios.body: A contested pace quickens the tempo, and the race becomes a test of raw speed and class rather than stamina, favouring the sharper-actioned prominent types who respond to a frantic early fraction.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the leaders and a hold-up performer finds a clear run in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Morehampton or Alfred Tennyson, natural hold-up types who can genuinely race from the rear, would need a truly strong pace to close the gap — plausible but dependent on Send Harry setting a faster gallop than his history suggests.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Complete Upset — Outsider Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If pace collapses or a midfield horse produces an unexpected career-best on the Firm surface.
scenarios.body: Ocean Echo or Inishfallen would need career-best efforts and significant assistance from a chaotic race shape to feature at the business end on current form.

watchPoints.text: Send Harry's early tempo is the fulcrum of this race — if he bowls along comfortably unchallenged, the race shape locks in for prominent types and any hold-up horse faces a near-impossible task.
Dancing Saxon's 155-day absence must be respected; if JP O'Brien has him cherry-ripe he is a major danger in the prominent position, but a ring-rusty effort would collapse Scenario A rapidly.

Morehampton carries the highest OR in the field (79) and a 5lb penalty relative to several rivals — if the pace is not strong enough to bring him into the race from behind, his top weight burden compounds the style disadvantage.

Tokyo Treasure's 273-day layoff combined with the specific form note of fading in the finish makes him a horse to watch for market moves rather than a logical race-shape beneficiary — any significant support would be informative.

Western Bandit's optimal trip appears to be 10f based on his recent campaign; connections dropping him sharply to 6½f on Firm ground is a move worth monitoring, as it could signal either a tactical experiment or a fitness spin.

races.name: Ei Electronics Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: I'm Spartacus
runners_data.note: Won over C&D (6f Gowran) and has Leading form at sprint trips on good ground; races as a front-runner naturally but flagged [STYLE_FIT] for this prominent mapping — in a lone-leader role it is far more dangerous and sets every fraction here; 10 days since last run is fine for a five-year-old in form.
runners_data.comment: I'm Spartacus won three starts back and has been a fairly consistent finisher either side of it, without threatening to repeat that level. Quick back into action just 10 days after his latest race over today's trip, he rates 68 with us, second of seventeen from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Rappell
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a placed effort over 7f at Gowran recently; going is fine but coming from the rear in a race not forecast to truly burn up presents a challenge; blinkers off, which is worth noting; stable has had a quiet 14-day period.
runners_data.comment: Rappell hasn't managed to win in his last six starts and hasn't finished inside the top five in that time, but a strong recorded speed figure of 74 hints at more upside than the bare results suggest. That form still sees him rated 70 with us, the highest in this field, backed by a quick 10-day turnaround and experience over today's trip from stall 2.

runners_data.name: Friars Gate
runners_data.note: Has a fade flagged in its profile and its last five runs have all been over 8f on soft or good ground — this step back to 6½f on firm is a significant concern for stamina-to-speed conversion; trainer has minimal recent winners.
runners_data.comment: Friars Gate is yet to win in her last five starts, with a fourth her only form of note among a run of modest finishes. Back 22 days after her latest race, she rates a middling 51 with us, tenth of seventeen from stall 4.

runners_data.name: Undefeatable
runners_data.note: Two-year-old form shows a win at Gowran but hasn't run for 260 days — a serious absence flag and fitness must be questioned; hold-up style and the overcrowded rear of this field make it hard to fancy on return.
runners_data.comment: Undefeatable won four starts back and has been a fair finisher either side of it, with a third among his placings. He's had a lengthy 260 days off since but has raced over today's trip before, rated 57 by us and seventh of seventeen from stall 11.

runners_data.name: Notforalongtime
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran running from hold-up position; form figures include a couple of thirds over 7-8f at Gowran, and the drop to 6½f is sharper than preferred; the pace headgear (p) is retained and stable has run just three horses in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Notforalongtime is yet to win in his last six starts, though back-to-back thirds are his form highlight among a run of modest finishes. He returns 22 days after his latest race over today's trip, rated 58 with us, fourth of seventeen from stall 15.

runners_data.name: Monastere
runners_data.note: Recent winner over 6f at Gowran is a solid positive, and it placed second over the same course and distance — the best recent sprint form in the hold-up/midfield group; headgear not listed, 10 days since last run, genuine 6f performer.
runners_data.comment: Monastere won last time out and was runner-up before that, though three unplaced efforts further back temper the overall picture. Quick back into action just 10 days after that latest race over today's trip, he's rated only 44 by us, sixteenth of seventeen from stall 9 despite the improving finish.

runners_data.name: El Fontenaro
runners_data.note: Placed second over 6f at Gowran last time, which is directly relevant course and trip form; natural prominent racer who should sit just off I'm Spartacus and is well-suited by this controlled gallop on fast ground; 29 days since last run is acceptable.
runners_data.comment: El Fontenaro is yet to win in her last five starts, though a second among them is the standout effort. Back 29 days after her latest race over today's trip, she's rated 58 with us, sixth of seventeen from stall 10, with a strong recorded speed figure of 77 catching the eye.

runners_data.name: Snap Decision
runners_data.note: Form figures on preferred distances are weak (8s, 8s, 7f) and fades are flagged; its true hold-up nature means it has been pushed to midfield on the map but is unlikely to get the run of things from there — a STYLE_FIT discount applies and the fade flag compounds concerns.
runners_data.comment: Snap Decision is yet to win in his last five starts, unable to better sixth in that spell. Quick back into action just 11 days after his latest race over today's trip, he's rated a middling 52 with us, ninth of seventeen from stall 6.

runners_data.name: Jazzy Dancer
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old who has won at 6-7f on good-to-soft but genuine hold-up style mapped to midfield due to field congestion; pace headgear retained; last ran 31 days ago; needs a pace collapse that is not forecast here to deliver its best.
runners_data.comment: Jazzy Dancer won five starts back. A runner-up effort four starts back followed, but his form has cooled since through three modest finishes. Back 31 days after his latest race over today's trip, he rates 59 with us, third of seventeen from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Banter
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for a stable that has had two winners in 14 days; placed second at Gowran over 6f and third and fourth at The Curragh — consistent sprint form and will push for the front end; tongue tie and blinkers worn; 36-day break is the slight concern.
runners_data.comment: Sovereign Banter is yet to win in his last five starts, but a second, a fourth and a third among his other finishes show he's frequently competitive. Back 36 days after his latest race over today's trip, he rates 58 with us, fifth of seventeen from stall 3.

runners_data.name: Dc Diva
runners_data.note: Only three career runs showing, all modest, with a fade flagged; genuine hold-up type shunted to midfield on the map — finds itself out of role and form offers very little encouragement on sprint trips on fast ground.
runners_data.comment: Dc Diva is yet to win in her last three starts, twice unplaced and no better than sixth otherwise. Back 22 days after her latest race over today's trip, she rates a modest 51 with us, eleventh of seventeen from stall 13.

runners_data.name: Pick A Window
runners_data.note: Fade flagged and hold-up style mapped to midfield as a redistribution; last five finishes are all double-digit positions; the 7f Gowran run (5th) is the one snippet of promise but context is weak overall, and its true running style will leave it last-to-hit the line here.
runners_data.comment: Pick A Window is yet to win in his last five starts, with a fifth his only finish of note among four unplaced efforts. Back 31 days after his latest race over today's trip, he's rated only 48 by us, fourteenth of seventeen from stall 1.

runners_data.name: Snowballs
runners_data.note: Consistent 5-6th finisher at sprint trips with a fade flag; pace headgear retained; hold-up type pushed into midfield framing — last ran 17 days ago which is fine, but the positive angle is limited on this trip and ground combination.
runners_data.comment: Snowballs is yet to win in his last five starts, with a fifth his best of a consistently modest run. Back 17 days after his latest race over today's trip, he's rated 49 by us, thirteenth of seventeen from stall 17, though a decent recorded speed figure of 69 offers a shred of hope.

runners_data.name: Hastily
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a string of zeros and 13th, 14th, 15th, 16th finishes in its last five; fade flagged and genuine hold-up type out of natural position; no realistic case to make here on any evidence.
runners_data.comment: Hastily is yet to win in her last five starts, rarely troubling the judge with only a ninth to show among four unplaced efforts. Back 29 days after her latest race over today's trip, she's rated 50 by us, twelfth of seventeen from stall 16.

runners_data.name: Whatswrongnow
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with a second over 6f at Gowran in recent history and ran just eight days ago — freshness is not a concern but recovery must be monitored; no jockey listed which is a soft flag; will push forward and be a factor in the lead group.
runners_data.comment: Whatswrongnow is yet to win in his last six starts, though two runner-up efforts and a third show he's frequently involved in the finish. Quick back into action just 8 days after his latest race over today's trip, he rates 54 with us, eighth of seventeen from stall 8.

runners_data.name: Gobi Star
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with a long string of zeros and double-digit finishes; fade flagged and hold-up type redistributed out of its natural rear-of-field role; trainer has had just one winner in 14 days from 14 runners — no angle to construct.
runners_data.comment: Gobi Star is yet to win in his last six starts, unplaced in five of them with only a seventh to his name. Back 31 days after his latest race over today's trip, he's rated 44 by us, fifteenth of seventeen from stall 12.

runners_data.name: Bel Espoir
runners_data.note: Fade flagged and recent form is 0-9-0-0-0-8; ran eight days ago in a five-runner field; hold-up style mapped to midfield due to overcrowding — the redistribution and fade tag combine to make its chance very limited on this fast 6½f track.
runners_data.comment: Bel Espoir is yet to win in her last six starts, unplaced in four of them with only an eighth and a ninth to show. Quick back into action just 8 days after her latest race over today's trip, she's rated bottom of the field on 34 from stall 7, though a strong recorded speed figure of 76 stands out.

races.paceDynamic: I'm Spartacus is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure it, should dictate on its own terms from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo on firm ground over 6½f at Limerick. El Fontenaro, Sovereign Banter, and Whatswrongnow are genuine prominent types who will look to sit just off the pace, creating a small lead group that nonetheless won't turn this into a true burn-up. The absence of a pace duel means the fractions are unlikely to be extreme, which in turn will not soften the ground for closers late — horses racing handy and able to produce a sustained run from 2f out are best placed to capitalise. Several runners — Snap Decision, Jazzy Dancer, Pick A Window, Dc Diva, Snowballs, Hastily, Gobi Star, and Bel Espoir — are true hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear of the field is overcrowded, meaning they are unlikely to get a clear run in time from their actual race position; the prominent berths will be controlled by I'm Spartacus, El Fontenaro, Sovereign Banter, and Whatswrongnow. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or just off the controlled leader — those tracking I'm Spartacus without burning energy are the profile to follow.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If I'm Spartacus dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and the prominent trackers swoop inside the final 2f.
scenarios.body: I'm Spartacus sets fractions that suit the chasing prominent group, with El Fontenaro and Sovereign Banter ideally placed to challenge as the field fans out on firm ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If the firm ground and steady fractions allow I'm Spartacus to sustain its lead all the way to the line.
scenarios.body: With no pace rival to force it wide or burn it early, I'm Spartacus controls the race from the front and the closing runners find the gap has not opened sufficiently on the fast surface.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group goes quicker than expected in the early stages and ties themselves up late.
scenarios.body: A faster-than-anticipated gallop from the lead trio would create a gap for midfield runners like Monastere or Rappell to weave through in the closing stages, though most mapped midfielders are true hold-up types who may not find a clear enough passage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If there is significant traffic trouble in the prominent group and a hold-up horse finds a gap late on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Given that the bulk of true hold-up types are mapped to midfield out of their natural role and that fast ground shortens the finishing straight window, this scenario requires a combination of pace collapse and clean passage that is unlikely to materialise.

watchPoints.text: I'm Spartacus is the only true front-runner and if it controls fractions entirely on its own terms from flag to finish, the race could be over before the prominent trackers get organised — watch whether El Fontenaro or Sovereign Banter push up to challenge early or concede the lead unopposed.

Sovereign Banter and El Fontenaro will both attempt to occupy the same prominent berths just off I'm Spartacus — if they bump or cover each other in the first 2f, the tactical advantage of their position is negated and I'm Spartacus benefits further.

The cluster of redistributed hold-up types (Snap Decision, Pick A Window, Dc Diva, Hastily, Gobi Star, Bel Espoir) mapped to midfield will create significant traffic and pocketing from the 3f pole — watch for horses trapped wide burning extra ground on firm.
Whatswrongnow ran just 8 days ago and no jockey has been confirmed — monitor the declaration closely and check for any fitness or market drift signal before post time.

Monastere's recent 6f Gowran win makes it the standout form horse among the hold-up/midfield group — if it can weave through a gap between the 2f and 1f poles it is the one true hold-up runner capable of landing Scenario C.

races.name: DAR Golf And Mann Family Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Zheleznaya Dama
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Brendan Duke with a flagged tendency to fade in the finish; dropping from 7-8f trips at the Curragh to this 6½f suggests the trip may be sharp enough to see her out, and her recent form string of 0083-P does little to inspire confidence in the finish she would need from deep.|
runners_data.comment: A third among a mixed run of results keeps Zheleznaya Dama interesting, and our figures rate her above her official mark. She races over a trip she has covered before, fresh after 27 days off, though the pulled-up effort in that sequence is the concern.

runners_data.name: Baby Basma
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3yo for E J O'Neill off a 79-day break, with her sole win coming at 5f — the step up to 6½f is a query, but Gavin Ryan takes the mount and she has shown ability in stronger company at The Curragh; form 1-47 leaves plenty of unknown.|
runners_data.comment: Baby Basma won three starts back and our figures rate her narrowly top of this field at 72, well above her official mark. She could finish only seventh last time out, and a 79-day absence adds to the concerns, though she has covered today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Princess Chloe
runners_data.note: Apprentice-ridden hold-up filly returning after 134 days off for Daniel Murphy; tongue-tie applied and all her starts have been at Sligo or The Curragh over 5-7f, so this Limerick 6½f is a fresh test — the long layoff is the primary concern.|
runners_data.comment: Princess Chloe has managed nothing better than fourth in four recent starts and is yet to win in that sequence, sitting below her official mark on our figures. She wears a tongue-tie and has covered today's trip before, but a 134-day absence is a concern.

runners_data.name: Spirit Above
runners_data.note: Active yard with Kevin Smith sending out 2 winners from 4 runners in the last 14 days, and Dylan Browne McMonagle is a significant booking for this hold-up filly; tongue-tie and pads previously worn, last run just 22 days ago, and the form placed second over 5f at the Curragh suggests she handles fast conditions — best of the closers if a clear run materialises.|
runners_data.comment: Spirit Above has yet to win in five recent starts but a second among them, along with a rating nudging above his official mark, keeps him competitive. Wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, he returns over a trip he has covered before having run just 22 days ago.

runners_data.name: Dawn Flame
runners_data.note: True hold-up operator whose recent form is largely at 8-10f and who is squeezed into midfield here because the map cannot place the volume of closers at the rear; the step down to 6½f is a significant trip shortening, and the ⚠ fade flag alongside an 0-13 trainer strike rate in 14 days makes this a hard proposition.|
runners_data.comment: Dawn Flame won earlier in this six-race sequence but found little there since, following an eighth-placed effort just 10 days ago wearing a tongue-tie and cheekpieces. He rates above his official mark and returns over a trip he has covered before.

runners_data.name: Jampa Ling
runners_data.note: The race's only confirmed front-runner, stepping up marginally in trip for Kieran Cotter off a 29-day break; Scott McCullagh has the keys to an uncontested lead on firm ground, and while the STYLE_FIT tag notes slight positional adjustment, Jampa Ling is the one horse who can dictate terms — form 159630 shows previous placed effort at this C&D trip.|
runners_data.comment: Jampa Ling's figure sits well clear of his official mark, built on a win towards the back of this six-race sequence, though he has been workmanlike since, most recently below-par 29 days ago. He returns over a trip he has covered before and remains a threat.

runners_data.name: Sayonara
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's consistent yard (5/36 in 14 days) sends this genuine hold-up filly who will find herself in a congested midfield rather than her natural position off the pace; form 8-5300 with a placed effort over 6f at Sligo gives some hope, but Ava Maher (10lb claimer) and the tactical compromise are negatives.|
runners_data.comment: Sayonara is yet to win in five recent starts, his last two below-par, though a third earlier in that sequence shows ability. He sits a touch above his official mark on our figures and returns over a trip he has covered before, 17 days on.

runners_data.name: Ochtar Againn
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up type whose headgear note (p) and repeated fade flag make her difficult to recommend; shuffled into midfield rather than her preferred rear position, and form figures of -00500 with all five recent runs ending in the bottom half suggest she needs things to go very right — she won't get the tactical setup she needs here.|
runners_data.comment: Ochtar Againn is yet to win in five recent starts, a fifth her best effort, and our figures leave her below her official mark. Wearing cheekpieces, she returns over a trip she has covered before but needs more to feature in this company.

runners_data.name: Dialin For Dollars
runners_data.note: Returning from a 282-day absence for David Marnane, this 2yo is by some distance the youngest in the field and has only seen soft or standard going in her history — firm is an unknown surface, and the long layoff combined with the natural hold-up style being displaced into midfield makes her a spectator's interest at best.|
runners_data.comment: Dialin For Dollars is yet to win in four starts but our figures rate him a big improver on his official mark and a leading contender. He has covered today's trip before, though a 282-day absence since that last run is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Glen Breeze
runners_data.note: The most interesting prominent type in the race behind Jampa Ling; J M Sheridan takes the mount for Patrick Magee, last run just 10 days ago, and the form 760203 shows a second place over 6f at Ballinrobe on good — capable of tracking Jampa Ling and posing the most realistic threat to the leader from an adjacent position.|
runners_data.comment: Glen Breeze is yet to win in six recent starts but signed off with a third last time out, having also been runner-up earlier in the sequence. He rates well above his official mark, wears a tongue-tie and cheekpieces, and races over a trip he knows.

runners_data.name: He's Holding Court
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery's second runner, with the yard in strong form (3/27 in 14 days), but this hold-up horse carries a fade flag and recent form 807640 screams consistency in defeat; Jack Cleary (5lb) rides, and like many in this race he'll be squeezed into midfield traffic rather than finding his natural rearward berth.|
runners_data.comment: This filly is yet to win in her last six starts, unplaced last time out with only a fourth to show at best. She sits above her official mark on our figures and returns over a trip she has covered before.

runners_data.name: Windsor Lily
runners_data.note: Blinkers fitted for Joseph Murphy and a fade flag to note; form 8-5900 at Limerick and elsewhere is not encouraging, and while she is a natural hold-up type she has been unable to produce a finish from her preferred position in recent starts — this race shape doesn't change that.|
runners_data.comment: Windsor Lily is yet to win in five recent starts, following a pair of unplaced efforts including 38 days ago. She does sit above her official mark on our figures, wears blinkers, and returns over a trip she has covered before, but the form is modest throughout.

runners_data.name: Iryna's Star

runners_data.comment: Iryna's Star is yet to win in six recent starts, with two fifth-placed efforts her best form, and she is towards the foot of this field on our figures. She returns over a trip she has covered before, though a 67-day absence adds to the questions.

runners_data.name: Sand Art

races.paceDynamic: Jampa Ling is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 15-runner 0-60 handicap over 6½f at Limerick on firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Scott McCullagh's mount should bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo without being pressured into burning early fuel. Glen Breeze is the one prominent type capable of tracking Jampa Ling from the front tier, but the rest of the field is stacked with hold-up horses, many of whom will be unable to secure their natural position and will end up shuffled into midfield regardless. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Sayonara, Dawn Flame, Ochtar Againn, Dialin For Dollars, He's Holding Court, Windsor Lily and others are all genuine closers who will be racing in a compressed midfield pack, negating their ability to produce the kind of finishing kick that requires daylight and separation. A single uncontested front-runner on firm going over 6½f sets up a race that strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or just off the leader without expending energy fighting for position — the prominent-to-midfield profile with a clean passage is the one to concentrate on here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Jampa Ling Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling leads throughout at a controlled firm-ground tempo and Glen Breeze tracks in second, setting a race that never truly quickens.
scenarios.body: Jampa Ling bowls along from flag to flag on fast ground with no pressure from rivals, and the lack of any rival willing to take it up means the pace remains honest but not brutal, favouring the horse on the front end. Glen Breeze, tracking throughout in second, is ideally positioned to pounce if Jampa Ling tires, while the compressed hold-up pack behind are left needing a gap that may never materialise in time.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Draw Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling and Glen Breeze open a lead through the middle sections that the hold-up horses, racing in an overcrowded midfield, cannot close.
scenarios.body: The two prominent types build a margin that becomes decisive on firm going where closing runs are harder to sustain over the final furlong, and the hold-up horses — bunched together and unable to find clear runs — leave their challenges too late. Spirit Above, if travelling prominently rather than deep, and Baby Basma with her handler's record at the trip could make late inroads but find the deficit too large.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Navigate Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected and Jampa Ling sets a genuine clip that softens the front pair, allowing one well-positioned closer to thread a run.
scenarios.body: Even under this scenario the closers must find a gap through the packed midfield of redistributed hold-up types, and only the sharpest, most efficiently produced finisher will get there in time on this firm surface. Spirit Above, with trainer Kevin Michael Smith in a 2/4 T14 spell and Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard, is best equipped to make a late strike if produced with a decisive run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If Jampa Ling goes too hard early on firm ground, capitulates in the final furlong, and the entire field concertinas in a scramble.
scenarios.body: With most runners racing out of their true hold-up role and compressed into midfield, the race becomes a lottery of who finds space first in the closing stages, and the lower-weighted runners like Iryna's Star or Sand Art could fluke a placing. However, this scenario is the least likely given the single-pace-setter dynamic and the absence of any strong pace rival to force a suicidal gallop.

watchPoints.text: Jampa Ling — if Scott McCullagh elects to drop in or the horse misses the break, the entire race shape collapses as there is no other confirmed front-runner to take up the running, leaving the whole field without a guide pace.

Glen Breeze — watch where J M Sheridan positions this horse in the early stalls; if Glen Breeze sits second and travels smoothly, it becomes the most dangerous horse in the race and the clearest threat to Jampa Ling at the line.

Spirit Above — Dylan Browne McMonagle's handling of this hold-up filly in the early stages is crucial; if she gets caught behind a wall of the redistributed midfield horses at the 4f pole, no amount of ability will deliver a clear run in time on firm ground.

Overcrowded midfield — with seven or more horses racing out of their natural hold-up position and compressed between the 3f and 5f markers, watch for significant traffic interference and pocket-riding issues from the 3f pole inward; horses drawn widest have the clearest passage and a positional advantage worth noting.

Firm ground and trip — all previous runs for Dawn Flame, Sand Art and Dialin For Dollars have come on soft or standard surfaces; their ability to handle firm ground over 6½f is genuinely unproven and worth factoring into any assessment before post time.

races.paceDynamic: She's Ideal is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 14-runner flat apprentice handicap over 1m4½f on firm ground at Limerick, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, she is set to dictate a controlled, uncontested gallop from the front. Deluca Chop, the only other prominent-style runner, will likely track in second, meaning the tempo is unlikely to be truly searching on this fast surface — a scenario that plays directly into the hands of the leader and horses close to the pace. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Metamorpheus, Magna Gee Gee, Faerie Tales, Eye Contact, Without Love and others are genuine hold-up horses displaced into a midfield mapping because there is simply no room for all of them to operate from the rear in the same race shape; of these, Metamorpheus and Without Love are most likely to actually secure a position closer to the pace given their recent form profiles. On a flat track with firm going and a lone front-runner controlling a steady pace, this race shape strongly favours prominent runners and those able to track the leader into the straight rather than deep closers relying on a truly run race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: She's Ideal Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If She's Ideal is allowed to dictate a controlled tempo throughout with Deluca Chop tracking and no serious pace pressure from behind.
scenarios.body: She's Ideal controls the fractions on firm ground, saves plenty for the straight, and a prolonged steady gallop means hold-up horses face a wall of pace into the final furlong; Deluca Chop, hardened by six recent runs in winning and placing form, is best placed to pounce if She's Ideal ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pick Up Scraps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that the hold-up horses find a wall of horses at the two-furlong pole, but a few athletic types find a way through late.
scenarios.body: Metamorpheus, a recent winner at 10f on soft who handles various ground, is the most likely true hold-up horse to find daylight; Without Love, in fine form over 12f on good-to-soft, also possesses the late gear to threaten if gaps appear in the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Mid-Race Injection Unsettles Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Deluca Chop or another prominent type applies meaningful pressure mid-race, forcing She's Ideal into a faster-than-comfortable pace.
scenarios.body: A contested early-to-mid gallop on firm ground would stretch the field, and a horse with stamina reserves would benefit; Deluca Chop's recent winning form over 13f on soft and good gives her the class and conditioning to press and outstay.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsiders Gate-Crash
scenarios.trigger: If the race breaks down chaotically, the pace collapses late, and lower-rated runners find themselves in the right place at the right time.
scenarios.body: Young Churchill or God Of Thunder, both hold-up types with race-fitness from recent runs at extended trips, could hit a place if fortuitous gaps open; this is the least structured scenario and is unlikely given the clean pace map.

watchPoints.text: She's Ideal's stamina at 1m4½f is unproven — watch whether she shortens up appreciably in the final two furlongs, as any weakness there would gift the race to Deluca Chop tracking directly behind.

Metamorpheus is a genuine hold-up horse who will race further back than his mapped position suggests — watch his position at the home turn, as any traffic he encounters on the inside could cost him his one realistic chance of getting competitive.

Eye Contact returns from 282 days off and wears p-headgear — monitor his pre-race behaviour and early race jumping, as an unfit or unsettled reappearance at this trip on firm would confirm him as a non-factor.

With this many hold-up types displaced toward midfield, watch the first two furlongs for jostling as Metamorpheus, Without Love, Magna Gee Gee and others fight for better-than-expected positions — any scrambling could compromise several runners simultaneously.

Deluca Chop wears the visor that has coincided with her two recent wins — watch whether apprentice Paddy Harnett tracks She's Ideal closely or allows a gap, as the tactical decision at the three-furlong pole could be decisive in this pace scenario.

His trainer is in good form, successful with 11 of the last 33 runners (33%) over the past fortnight. Back after a 43-day absence, our rating of 73 (4th of 6, speed 60) keeps him right in contention.

runners_data.name: Lamberella
runners_data.note: David Marnane's filly has a poor recent sequence including a tenth-place finish, carries a fade-in-finish flag, and while her true running style is hold-up she has been mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear; her trainer has zero wins from eleven runners in the last 14 days, compounding the structural disadvantage.|
runners_data.comment: Lamberella was unplaced last time out, following an 8th two starts back and a better effort of 5th three starts prior; she is yet to win in her last five starts. She returns 30 days after that latest run; rated only 68 here (6th of 6, speed 68), the outsider on these figures with little in the profile to inspire confidence.

races.paceDynamic: Hassaniya is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-horse field over 1m4½f on firm ground at Limerick, and with no genuine rival to press them early, they are likely to control tempo from the outset and dictate a sustainable, measured gallop. Gaelic Drills and Maxminelli are unclassified in style but neither has a demonstrated record of making the running, so Hassaniya should enjoy an uncontested lead and set the fractions entirely to their own liking. Themis, Bell Ex Too, and Lamberella are hold-up types who will be dependent on the pace being strong enough to close into, but with one relatively modest front-runner setting a controlled tempo on firm going, the race is likely to be won from the front or just off it rather than from the rear. This race shape strongly favours prominent or pace-pressing profiles — horses able to sit within a length or two of Hassaniya and kick from there — because the hold-up brigade face a scenario where there simply may not be enough early gallop to reel in a front-runner who has never been asked a serious question. The field holds more hold-up types than can all get a productive late run, and Lamberella is the runner most compromised by the likely slow-burn shape given its redistribution from the rear to midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Hassaniya Leads, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya dictates a controlled pace unchallenged and kicks clear before the hold-up horses can mount a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: Hassaniya bowls along in front on firm Limerick ground, and with no rival able to pressurise them early, they control every yard of the race and simply have to handle the extra distance of 1m4½f.
winners: A horse with pace-pressing ability tracking Hassaniya's every move is ideally placed to challenge
but any hold-up runner will need an extraordinary turn of foot to overhaul a front-runner who has never been tested.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Presser Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent tracker sits just off Hassaniya throughout and produces a strong sustained challenge in the final two furlongs on firm ground.
scenarios.body: Gaelic Drills or Maxminelli, sitting in the slipstream of Hassaniya, uses the firm going to quicken past the leader approaching the final furlong as fatigue begins to show.
winners: This scenario suits a horse with tactical versatility who can produce a clean
straight gallop late — the unclassified pair have each shown recent form at this trip and may be better suited to it than their ratings suggest.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finishes Fast
scenarios.trigger: If Hassaniya sets a genuinely strong early tempo rather than the anticipated dawdle, creating a proper gallop that enables a late run.
scenarios.body: Themis or Bell Ex Too, able to produce a genuine late flourish if the pace is honest, picks up ground in the straight as the leader ties up.
winners: The firm ground suits a horse with a clean action
but both hold-up runners carry the concern of fading in the finish
and a slow-burn pace makes this scenario structurally unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Lamberella Overcomes Role
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses entirely mid-race and Lamberella, mapped to midfield from a true hold-up position, can capitalise on a chaotic shape.
scenarios.body: Lamberella would need a fundamentally different race shape to its expected run, essentially reversing the tactical setup — the horse has a fade-in-finish flag and a poor recent form string including a last-of-ten.
winners: Racing out of its natural role and carrying the lowest OR in the field
this is a low-probability outcome dependent on multiple things going wrong for the more fancied runners.

watchPoints.text: Hassaniya's true role is prominent rather than a natural front-runner — watch for any early signs they drift off the pace or fail to stride forward cleanly, as this would undermine the entire race shape projected.|

Maxminelli is fitted with a hood today and has the most consistent recent form at the trip — if W J Lee opts to press Hassaniya early rather than sit off, this could turn into a genuine two-horse battle that changes the pace entirely.|

Themis and Lamberella both carry a fade-in-finish flag, so even if the pace unexpectedly quickens and brings them into contention, watch for them stopping in the final furlong on this firm Limerick surface.|

The going has been consistently Firm across all seven races today at Limerick — there is no track-freshening element to factor in, and runners with confirmed good/firm form should be preferred over those whose best form has come on softer surfaces.|
